newsitem.title: NEPAL: Earthquake rocks Nepal, no casualties reported.
newsitem.headline: Earthquake rocks Nepal, no casualties reported.

text.p: An earthquake measuring 4.6 on the open-ended Richter scale rocked Nepal's Kathmandu valley on Monday, triggering panic among residents in the region but there were no immediate reports of casualties, officials said.
The National Seismological centre said the epicentre of the earthquake, which struck at 6.28 a.m. (0143 GMT), was in Rasuwa district, northeast of Kathmandu.
The district was also rocked by two earthquakes and several tremors on Saturday.
"It is a lower, medium-size quake and could be the aftershock of Saturday's tremors," Ramlochan Prasad Tandukar, the Seismological centre's geologist, told Reuters.
Officials said no reports of casualties had been received from the region but some houses in Rasuwa and neighbouring Nuwakot and Sindhupalchowk districts had developed cracks.
The region was hit by several shocks on Saturday with the main tremor measuring 5.8 on the Richter scale also felt in Kathmandu, capital of the tiny Himalayan kingdom.
Police said residents in the Rasuwa district were spending the nights in makeshift shelters outside their homes, fearing worse jolts could follow.
Earthquakes between five and six on the Richter scale are powerful enough to cause heavy damage in populated areas.
More than 700 people were killed when an earthquake measuring 6.5 on the Richter scale hit Udayapur in eastern Nepal in 1988.
